samples.summary: Share-link note image-upload failures are silent — the raw uploader throws and nothing reports it to the visitor
samples.evidence: `uploadImage` is `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` (image-insert.ts:40), whose returned function `await postShareTokenImage(...)` **throws** on any non-OK response (api/images.ts:51-62) and never toasts. The notes engine's `beginUpload` treats a rejection as "the host already reported this": `const failed = (err) => { console.error(...); return null; }` (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:179-190), so the placeholder is removed and `insertImage` skipped with only a console entry. Every other mount wraps the uploader: `notes-detail.tsx:208-231` catches and `toast.error`s, and the shared *docs* mount goes through `insertImageFromFile`, which toasts (image-insert.ts:144-151). So an editor-role share visitor who pastes an oversized/rejected/network-failed image sees the "Uploading…" ghost vanish with no explanation and no image.

samples.summary: Divider drag does not compensate for the grab offset inside the now-25px divider, so the hairline snaps ~12px away from the finger on the first move
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth; ... const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track` sets the *editor pane's* width (and hence the divider's LEFT edge) to the pointer x. The painted hairline is the content box, centred inside 12px of padding on each side, so after the first `pointermove` the visible line sits ~12.5px to the right of the pointer. Widening the box from 7px to 25px multiplies this systematic offset by ~3.6 and produces a visible snap at drag start, since the user grabs the hairline (the divider's centre) but the code re-anchors to its left edge. Recording `e.clientX - divider.getBoundingClientRect().left` at pointerdown and subtracting it in `onMove` is what makes the pane boundary track the grabbed point.

samples.summary: `track` can be zero/negative, making `splitRatio` NaN and permanently writing `NaN%` flex bases
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth;` — when the container is not laid out (width 0, e.g. a hidden/detached mount, or jsdom where `offsetWidth` is 0 and `rect.width` is 0), `track` is 0. `(ev.clientX - rect.left) / 0` is `NaN` when the numerator is also 0, and `Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.85, NaN))` is `NaN`, so `splitRatio` becomes NaN for the lifetime of the editor: both `onMove` and every later `applyViewMode` then emit `flex: 1 1 NaN%`, which the browser discards, leaving the split panes stuck at their previous/unstyled widths. The pre-change code divided by `rect.width`, which had the same zero-width hazard but no second subtraction; a clamp such as `Math.max(1, rect.width - divider.offsetWidth)` plus a `Number.isFinite(ratio)` guard would close it.

samples.summary: A viewer-role share visitor now inherits the stored vim keymap with no control to leave it
samples.evidence: `const [keymap, setKeymap] = useState<NoteKeymap>(readKeymap);` seeds the keymap for both roles, but `NotesToolbar` renders the keymap dropdown only under `{!readOnly && (...)}` (notes-toolbar.tsx:549). The previous shared mount passed no `keymap` at all, so a viewer always got `default` (notes-view.tsx:99 default). After this change a visitor who once selected Vim in the workspace route opens every read-only share link in vim mode — arrow/Home/End behaviour and key handling change — with no menu entry to switch back. Either keep the keymap picker on read-only mounts (it is display-only, like the view menu) or do not seed vim when `readOnly`.

samples.summary: A failed toolbar chunk load takes the whole shared note surface down, not just the toolbar
samples.evidence: `<Suspense fallback={null}><NotesToolbar .../></Suspense>` wraps a `lazy()` import (line 19-23). A rejected dynamic import (stale hashed chunk after a deploy, offline blip) is rethrown by the lazy component and, with no error boundary anywhere between here and the route (`shared-document.tsx` mounts no boundary; `App.tsx:99` is a plain `Suspense`), React unmounts the whole subtree — including the sibling `NotesView` and the attached Yorkie document — leaving a blank page for a visitor who was mid-edit. A local error boundary (or a retrying import) would degrade to "no toolbar" instead of "no page".

samples.summary: Reworded `showAuthors` doc cites the revision preview as a `NotesView` mount, but the revision preview never uses `NotesView` — the fallback is now unreachable
samples.evidence: The new comment says the stored-preference fallback is "kept for a mount that owns no view menu (the revision preview)". `revision-preview.tsx:746-759` mounts the engine directly (`initializeNote(container, store, resolvedTheme, true, 'view')`) and never renders `NotesView`. Grepping `NotesView` shows exactly two mounts — `notes-detail.tsx:319` and `shared-notes-layout.tsx:116` — and both now pass `showAuthors` explicitly, so `const [storedShowAuthors] = useState(readShowAuthors)` / `showAuthors ?? storedShowAuthors` (lines 107-108) is dead in every current caller and the justification given for keeping it is factually wrong.
